governing_note: F6 is cross-SOURCE composition. F7 is cross-WAVE temporal realization within a source family. They are ORTHOGONAL at the per-source and per-track level, and SERIAL only at the integrated whole-world claim.

cases.name: same survey, two comparable waves
cases.F7_required: REQUIRED — comparability authority + temporal key + delta + established directionality
cases.note: This is the pure F7 case and the core of what F7 can close independently.

cases.name: two surveys, same rough period, related proposition
cases.F7_required: NOT REQUIRED — no temporal claim without comparable waves
cases.note: Cross-source structural coexistence is lawful without any temporal claim.

cases.name: two surveys with nonaligned fieldwork intervals
cases.F6_required: REQUIRED — coexistence, with explicit non-alignment recorded
cases.F7_required: REQUIRED PER FAMILY, but cross-family temporal comparison is NOT lawful on interval evidence alone
cases.orthogonal_or_serial: ORTHOGONAL then BLOCKED at the cross-family join
cases.note: Mismatched fieldwork intervals must be represented as typed noncomparability, never coerced to a common midpoint. This is the case that exposes the time-grain fork.

cases.name: two surveys, each with its own temporal trajectory
cases.F6_required: REQUIRED — two tracks coexist in one world
cases.note: Historically impossible: V553 temporal identity required EXACTLY ONE survey family per report. Generalising the FUNCTION (declare the family) while dropping the topology (one family per report) is the key F6+F7 move.

cases.name: one source comparable through time, another single-wave only
cases.F6_required: REQUIRED — coexistence with asymmetric temporal standing
cases.F7_required: REQUIRED FOR THE COMPARABLE SOURCE ONLY
cases.note: A single-wave source contributes a structural field with NO temporal track. SINGLE_WAVE_PRESSURE != TEMPORAL_PRESSURE_FIELD forbids inventing one.

cases.name: conflicting temporal movement across sources
cases.F6_required: REQUIRED — and the conflict is the payload
cases.note: Disagreement must be preserved as a typed contradiction relation. SOURCE_CONFLICT != AVERAGE_BY_DEFAULT forbids averaging it away.

cases.name: temporal relation blocked by noncomparability, cross-source structural coexistence still lawful
cases.orthogonal_or_serial: ORTHOGONAL — F7 failure does not block F6
cases.note: The decisive case for orthogonality: a blocked temporal relation must not contaminate the lawful cross-source structural relation.

orthogonality_consequences.F6_does_not_require_F7: Cases B and G are F6-complete with no temporal claim at all.
orthogonality_consequences.F7_does_not_require_F6: Case A is F7-complete within one survey family with no cross-source claim.
orthogonality_consequences.serial_only_at: the integrated whole-PRE-V3 world claim (F5+F6+F7+F8 composed), never between the two gates as such.

PRIOR_HQ_PHRASE_ADJUDICATION.phrase: F7 cannot honestly close before F6.
PRIOR_HQ_PHRASE_ADJUDICATION.finding: The phrase is wrong as a dependency claim and right as a warning about COMPLETION.
why_wrong_as_dependency: F7's own binding law is defined WITHIN a survey family: 'comparable same-survey waves'. It never invokes cross-source composition. Case A is fully F7-completable alone.
F6's own binding law is defined WITHIN one objective world across sources. It never invokes temporal directionality. Cases B and G are fully F6-completable alone.

Case G shows the dependency runs the WRONG way for a claim: a REFUSED temporal relation must not block lawful cross-source coexistence. If F7 were a prerequisite for F6, G would be unsatisfiable whenever temporal comparison fails — which would force either a fabricated temporal result or the loss of a lawful structural one.
PRIOR_HQ_PHRASE_ADJUDICATION.why_right_as_warning: A WHOLE-PRE-V3 completion claim does need both, because the deliverable is one world that is simultaneously multi-source and temporally realized. A gate may be typed-negative at some scope (HQD-125 §12), so a project may legitimately hold F7 closed and F6 open.

F7_can_close_independently_on: any per-family temporal track, including several tracks at once (case D's F7 half)
typed noncomparability where comparability fails (case G's F7 half)
single-wave sources contributing no temporal product (case E's F7 half)
requires_actual_F6_plus_F7_composition: any cross-source claim that also asserts temporal movement (case F)
case C's cross-family comparison, if it is ever to be more than typed noncomparability
